solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Moths — dearie me! — got rampant

indicators.note: rampant means running wild and unchecked, so the letters are let loose into a new order

parts.note: the exclamation and the verb supply eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in dismay as moths run riot through the wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: GEOMETRIDAE is the scientific family of geometer moths, whose caterpillars are the looping inchworms.
explanation.definitionFit: The family name covers a large group of moth species, so it stands for moths collectively.

clue.text: God exciting last of the pagans, not the first

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so the gathered letters are stirred into a new order
not the first tells us to drop the opening letter of the word it follows
the last of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of this little word
taken as written before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: A god stirs the last of the pagans, though not the leading one, to fervour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last of the pagans' reads as one phrase, but 'last of' governs only 'the'; 'pagans, not the first' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganesa (Ganesh) is the elephant-headed Hindu deity of wisdom and new beginnings.

clue.text: Toss something round up — an old coin

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to lob is to toss in a high arc
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone flips a round object into the air: an old coin, as at a match's start.
explanation.definitionFit: An obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece, worth a sixth of a drachma.

clue.text: Trendy area in ruins — where the yacht clubs are

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the word that follows

parts.note: to mar is to spoil, so ruins gives the verb with S
in means fashionable
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A fashionable waterfront district lies wrecked, where the yacht clubs once stood.
explanation.definitionFit: Marinas are harbours for pleasure boats, the natural home of yacht clubs.

clue.text: Problem with major Christian festival — the time shifting

indicators.note: shifting tells us a letter is lifted from its place in the word and moved elsewhere

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
the feast of the Resurrection

explanation.surface: Someone has a problem with the date of Easter, which moves every year.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of EASTER moves from fourth place to the front, leaving the other letters in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a puzzle or tricky question, so it is another word for a problem.

clue.text: Read out liturgy outside church, having been lifted up

indicators.note: outside tells us the first word wraps around the word that follows

parts.note: a rite is a liturgical form of service

indicators.note: lifted up in a down entry means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A liturgy is read out on the church steps after being raised high.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to say aloud from memory or text, the same as reading something out.

clue.text: Slow speech an attraction to learner

parts.note: a draw is something that attracts crowds
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A teacher's slow way of talking appeals to a struggling pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a lazy manner of speaking with vowels drawn out, i.e. slow speech.

clue.text: Cleaner hair? See this fibre here appearing replenished

indicators.note: replenished suggests the letters are refilled and mixed again into a different arrangement
the fibre plus the word that appears alongside it make the jumble, so that word must be taken away to leave the fibre

parts.note: the two words supply the letters of the jumble
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: An advert promises cleaner hair from a synthetic fibre, freshly restocked here.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: the fibre's letters plus HERE, mixed, make CLEANER HAIR, so remove HERE from that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrilan is a trade name for an acrylic synthetic fibre used in clothing and carpets.

clue.text: Purpose of home nurse

definitions.note: used as a verb, to purpose

parts.note: in means at home
to tend is to nurse

explanation.surface: The aim of a nurse who works in people's own homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purpose' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in 'I purpose to go'.
explanation.definitionFit: To purpose something, in older English, is to have it as one's aim, which is to intend it.

clue.text: Chinese official, a fellow seen around Beijing primarily?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: seen around means the preceding letters are placed about the next piece

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the place name is wanted

parts.note: the initial of the capital

explanation.surface: A Chinese official is spotted travelling around the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a man around Beijing is only loosely a definition of a Chinese official.
explanation.definitionFit: An amban was a Manchu imperial resident or high official in places such as Tibet.

clue.text: Drink whisky maybe, then tear around? You'll get abuse

parts.note: malt whisky is one example of a drink

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about and spun into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Drink whisky and then rampage: a warning that abuse will follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To maltreat is to treat cruelly, the same as to abuse someone.

clue.text: Firm bound to receive audio signal

indicators.note: bound to means tied up within, so the first word is held inside the following one

parts.note: to earn is to receive as pay
CO is short for company

explanation.surface: A company is obliged to pick up a sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An earcon is a brief distinctive sound used by computers to signal an event, an audio counterpart of an icon.

clue.text: A cricket club ace laid into spoilt child in game

indicators.note: laid into means placed inside, so the first pieces go within the spoilt child

parts.note: a brat is a spoilt child
taken as written
CC is the abbreviation for cricket club
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A cricket club's star player lays into a spoilt child during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid into' suggests a telling-off, but it means the letters are set inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino card game in which players bet on the banker or the punter.

clue.text: Suppression of measure is restricting Greek character

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth length

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the preceding word encloses the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
psi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A rule that suppresses a Greek figure's freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellipsis is the omission of words from a sentence, a suppression of what is understood.

clue.text: Something oily I detect in bishop with purpose

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: in tells us the first phrase sits inside the word that comes later

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose
to see is to detect, so I detect gives I SEE

explanation.surface: A sleuth notices something greasy about a bishop with a purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop's B comes first; I SEE then goes inside END.
explanation.definitionFit: Beniseed is sesame seed, valued for the oil pressed from it.

clue.text: Shock of long ago — David's missile brought about alien's end

indicators.note: brought about means put around, so the missile wraps the last letter

parts.note: David killed Goliath with a stone from his sling

indicators.note: end points to the final letter of the word it is attached to

parts.note: the final letter of the word alien

explanation.surface: An ancient shock: David's slingshot felled the alien giant at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonne is an obsolete form of 'stun', to astonish or shock, so it is a shock of long ago.

clue.text: Mollusc Nellie found to the west of Torbay

indicators.note: the west of a word written across is its leftmost part, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the leftmost letter of the resort's name
Nellie is a pet form of the name Ellen

explanation.surface: A mollusc named Nellie turns up on the coast west of Torbay, a Devon resort area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To the west of Torbay' reads as a place on a map, but it only picks out Torbay's leftmost letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tellen is a variant spelling of tellin, a thin-shelled marine bivalve.

clue.text: Cunning needed to have a pound as a unit of weight

definitions.note: the answer is the plural of rotl, so strictly units

parts.note: art means craft or cunning
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)

explanation.surface: Shrewd trading demands a pound as a standard weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Artal is a plural of rotl, a Middle Eastern weight measure of roughly a pound.

clue.text: Word of thanks about a TV comedy series providing entertainment

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word of thanks goes round what follows

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
taken as written
M*A*S*H was the long-running sitcom set in a Korean War army hospital

explanation.surface: A thank-you note about a television comedy that gave viewers fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamasha is an Anglo-Indian word for a show, spectacle or commotion, i.e. entertainment.

clue.text: Second worker a bit useless?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: An assistant who is rather lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit useless' seems to mean slightly hopeless, but a bit is a coin: a shand is a worthless counterfeit one.
explanation.definitionFit: Shand is a Scots word for a base or counterfeit coin, a piece of money that is no good.

clue.text: Old-fashioned conduct of rescuer, new leader

indicators.note: a new leader means the opening letter of the word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a saviour is one who rescues

explanation.surface: The old-world manners of a rescuer who has taken over in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter replaces the S; the definition and crossers settle it as H.
explanation.definitionFit: Haviour is an obsolete shortening of behaviour, meaning conduct or demeanour.

clue.text: Meal giving minimum of enjoyment in Lent?

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the word that follows

parts.note: Lent is an example of a fast, hence the question mark

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is the least of it, here its single opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of enjoyment

explanation.surface: A meal offering the least pleasure during the Lenten season.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a meagre Lenten meal, yet the answer is the opposite: a feast.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast is a large celebratory meal.

clue.text: Economical father dealt with "superior" girl

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
U means upper-class, the superior social style
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A thrifty father handles a snooty girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Frugal means sparing with money or food, which is to be economical.

clue.text: Communist revolutionary, say, being transformed — no longer goes wild

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning around, so the word is read from the other end

parts.note: red is a common name for a communist

indicators.note: being transformed means changed in form, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A communist revolutionary, being changed, has stopped running riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Communist revolutionary' reads as one person, but 'revolutionary' is the instruction to turn the communist round.
explanation.definitionFit: Deray is an archaic verb meaning to act wildly or riotously, hence the 'no longer' in the definition.

clue.text: Sea-monster surfacing, catcher of fish — it's hairy

indicators.note: surfacing means rising up, which in a down entry reads the letters from the bottom

parts.note: an orc is a mythical sea-monster
a net catches fish

explanation.surface: A sea-monster rises and is caught by a fisherman's net, and it's hairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cronet is the band of hair growing over the top of a horse's hoof.

clue.text: It's heathen god I am following?

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds
contracted to I'm

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is a pagan god they are a follower of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am following' places I'M after the god.
explanation.definitionFit: Panim is an old word for a pagan or infidel, i.e. a heathen.

clue.text: Man of the cloth in car preceding Queen

parts.note: a Merc is a Mercedes car
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A clergyman driving ahead of the Queen's car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of the cloth' suggests a priest; here it is a cloth merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercer is a dealer in textiles, especially silks, so literally a man of the cloth.

clue.text: Like many a plant sheep devoured

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
ate is the past tense of eat

explanation.surface: A sheep has eaten the plants, as so often happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramate means branched, a description that fits a great many plants.

clue.text: Star's success embraced by everyone

indicators.note: embraced by means held within, so the first word sits inside the second

parts.note: all means everyone
a go is a success, as in make a go of it

explanation.surface: A star's triumph is applauded by everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star's' reads as a possessive, but it is 'star is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Algol is a well-known variable star in the constellation Perseus.

clue.text: Minister is wanting end of service to change

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister
taken as written

indicators.note: end of asks for the final letter only of the word after it

parts.note: the final letter of service

explanation.surface: A minister wants the closing part of the service altered.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise is to amend or alter, i.e. to change.

clue.text: Sketch-writer maybe supporting office secretary in record-keeping role?

parts.note: pro means in favour of
an office worker who files records, cryptically described

explanation.surface: A satirical writer who backs an office secretary keeping records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sketch-writer' suggests a comedy writer; it is someone who writes character sketches.
explanation.definitionFit: A profiler writes profiles, short biographical portraits, so is one kind of sketch-writer.

clue.text: Plant with bottom side turned over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: a keel is the bottom side of a ship

explanation.surface: A plant whose lower part has been flipped up.
explanation.definitionFit: The leek is a plant of the onion family, grown as a vegetable.

clue.text: Santa travelling with gig — a big mover seen above?

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters move into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Father Christmas flying in a horse-drawn carriage across the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: A gig is a light two-wheeled carriage, which fits the picture of Santa in transit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas giant is a huge planet such as Jupiter, a large body moving across the sky above us.

clue.text: An inauthentic person's loss of voice

parts.note: the indefinite article, shortened
a phony is a fake person

explanation.surface: A fraud has lost their voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphony (aphonia) is the medical term for an inability to produce speech sounds.

clue.text: Entreat outside wordsmith to provide material

indicators.note: outside means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: to sue is to plead or entreat
ED is short for editor, one who works with words

explanation.surface: Someone begs an author for some written material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like writing to supply, but it is a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with a napped finish, a material used for shoes and jackets.

clue.text: Young delinquent in the bar larks about

indicators.note: about means all around and out of order, so the letters get a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A young troublemaker fools about in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Halbstarker is a German loanword for a teenage hooligan, literally 'half-strong'.
